stem: Siddharth cycles 900 m to the park in 300 s. On the way home he covers the same 900 m in 150 s. His speed changes during both trips.

parts.text: What is his average speed on the way home compared with the trip to the park?

options.text: It doubles from 3 m/s to 6 m/s.
It halves from 3 m/s to 1.5 m/s.
It cannot be found, because his speed was not uniform.

parts.text: How is average speed found for a trip?

part_answers.answer: Total distance divided by total time for that trip.

teacher.key_rationale: Average speed is total distance over total time: 900/300 = 3 m/s to the park and 900/150 = 6 m/s home, so it doubles even when motion is not uniform. Halving reverses the time change; saying average speed cannot be found without uniform motion is a scope error.
